title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the Angular introduction, setup, first app, architecture, and CLI.

questions.question: What is Angular?
options: A platform and framework for building client‑side apps
questions.explanation: Angular is a full platform and framework for building Single Page Applications using HTML, CSS, and TypeScript.

questions.question: Which language is Angular primarily written in and used with?
questions.explanation: Angular uses TypeScript, a superset of JavaScript that adds static typing.

questions.question: AngularJS (1.x) and Angular (2+) are the same framework.
questions.explanation: AngularJS is the 1.x version written in JavaScript; Angular 2+ is a complete rewrite using TypeScript.

questions.question: What does SPA stand for?
questions.explanation: SPA stands for Single Page Application – an app that loads a single HTML page and dynamically updates content.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a core Angular building block?
questions.explanation: Promises are a JavaScript concept used in Angular, but not a core architectural building block like components, modules, services, templates, and directives.

questions.question: The command to globally install Angular CLI is: npm install -g ______
questions.explanation: The official package is `@angular/cli`.

questions.question: Which command creates a new Angular workspace?
questions.explanation: `ng new <project-name>` creates a new workspace.

questions.question: During `ng new`, what question does the CLI ask?
options: Would you like to add Angular routing?
Which version of Bootstrap to install?
questions.explanation: It asks whether to add routing and which stylesheet format to use.

questions.question: You need a paid license to use Angular CLI.
questions.explanation: Angular CLI is free and open source under the MIT license.

questions.question: What does the @Component decorator do?
options: Marks a class as an Angular component and provides metadata
questions.explanation: The @Component decorator tells Angular that the class is a component and supplies configuration like selector and template.

questions.question: Which file contains the root component of an Angular app?
questions.explanation: `app.component.ts` is the root component’s class file.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `{{ title }}` in an Angular template?
options: It displays the value of the `title` property (interpolation)
questions.explanation: Double curly braces are Angular’s interpolation syntax to display component data.

questions.question: `ng serve` automatically opens your default browser.
questions.explanation: By default it does not; you must use `ng serve --open` to auto‑open the browser.

questions.question: Which Angular module is required to run an app in a browser?
questions.explanation: `BrowserModule` provides services essential to launch and run a browser app.

questions.question: What is the role of `AppModule`?
options: It is the root module that bootstraps the application
questions.explanation: `AppModule` is the root NgModule that tells Angular how to assemble the application.

questions.question: A service is typically a ______ (shared across the app).
questions.explanation: Services provided in root are singletons – only one instance exists.

questions.question: Dependency Injection (DI) in Angular helps with:
options: Providing instances of services to components that need them
questions.explanation: DI automatically supplies services to components, keeping the code decoupled and testable.

questions.question: Where would you run `console.log()` to debug an Angular component?
questions.explanation: You add `console.log()` in the component’s TypeScript class; the output appears in the browser console.

questions.question: You cannot use Chrome DevTools to debug Angular apps.
questions.explanation: You can absolutely use DevTools; source maps even allow you to debug the original TypeScript code.

questions.question: Which command builds your Angular app for production?
questions.explanation: `ng build` compiles the app into an output directory (`dist/`). Adding `--prod` enables optimisations.
